markdown_report:
The recommended first experiment remains **joint lexical-residual HSTU**: enrich the corrected backbone’s item embeddings with title/description features learned from scratch. This targets two reported user failures: broad associations replacing specific intent, and overlooked connector/format/dimension distinctions. Benefits remain hypotheses; text cannot establish compatibility or identify fulfilled needs.

**Insights and directions.** The starting evidence suggests three insights: (1) Electronics warrants attention: its sampled wrong-rank rate is 10.71%, although training margins do not establish validation performance. (2) Collapse scores near 0.5 indicate approximately zero mean cosine similarity, so anti-collapse regularization lacks support. (3) Concrete textual distinctions could address reported specificity failures, but missing information remains unknown.

Related work suggests three further insights: (1) HSTU-BLaIR, TASTE, and Recformer support investigating content sharing, but their pretrained representations leave learning from scratch unresolved. (2) SimRec motivates textual supervision; TedRec cautions that direct ID/text addition can be ineffective. (3) Official HSTU supports multi-negative sampled softmax, while Hard-BPR highlights false-negative risks.

These form three directions: **representation specificity**, **candidate discrimination**, and **temporal relevance**.

**Framework and candidate assessment.** Scores are Originality / Potential / User alignment / Model alignment / Difficulty; higher difficulty means harder implementation. Benefits (+) and limitations (−) are hypotheses grounded in the supplied diagnoses.

| Idea | Scores | Critical assessment |
|---|---|---|
| A. Joint lexical-residual HSTU | 4/7/8/6/5 | Originality: + constrained adaptation, − established fusion. Potential: + sparse-item sharing, − weak lexical supervision. User: + specific attributes and compatibility clues, − no compatibility labels. Model: + Electronics discrimination, − unverified. Difficulty: + small encoder, − scale, caching, and checkpoint integration. |
| B. Larger uniform-negative sampled softmax | 3/6/4/8/3 | Originality: + targeted test, − standard objective. Potential: + ranking supervision, − diminishing returns. User: + candidate ordering, − no attribute evidence. Model: + weak separation, − margins may mislead. Difficulty: + existing scoring, − GPU cost. |
| C. Bucketed historical time bias | 3/6/7/4/5 | Originality: + task adaptation, − native HSTU mechanism. Potential: + recent intent, − imperfect recency proxy. User: + current purpose and stale demand, − completed needs unobserved. Model: + contextual discrimination, − no measured temporal failure. Difficulty: + internal bias, − timestamp plumbing. |

**Selected experiment.** At 0% progress, retain A for direct alignment with two user failures and Electronics’ weak separation. Preserve model identifiers and number-unit tokens. Add a small, scale-matched, jointly trained lexical residual to ID embeddings; retain HSTU, causal training, and the baseline objective. Use identical representations for histories and candidates.

Predeclare one baseline and one lexical configuration, preserving seeds, four-category routing, existing checkpoint schedule, 200-epoch ceiling, and 200 batches/epoch. Select the complete configuration by fixed macro validation HR@10; freeze one checkpoint/category. Log every evaluation and prefer baseline on ties. Sampled HR does not establish full-catalog quality [Krichene–Rendle]; repeated selection can overfit [Cawley–Talbot]. If host-provided per-user hits are available, report paired stratified bootstrap differences descriptively. Serialize architecture, vocabulary, buffers, and weights; mirror them in the predictor writer. No gains or user-behavior improvements are claimed before measurement.

idea.description: Joint lexical-residual HSTU: replace the baseline item-embedding lookup with one jointly trained module combining item identity and scale-matched pooled title/description tokens. Preserve the corrected HSTU backbone and baseline objective. Retain this as the first experiment; objective and temporal changes remain alternatives rather than simultaneous modifications.
idea.motivation: The user diagnosis identifies broad thematic matching and missed connector, format, and dimension distinctions. Public titles/descriptions may supply specific evidence, and shared lexical parameters may help discriminate sparse Electronics items, where sampled negative-over-positive errors reach 10.71%. These are plausible mechanisms, not demonstrated effects. Content absence, compatibility, completed needs, and actual willingness to choose an item cannot be inferred reliably from lexical similarity or HR@10. Scores remain originality 4 and future potential 7; implementation difficulty increases from 4 to 5 because correct scaling, effective embeddings, caching, and predictor consistency require care.
idea.implementation_notes:
Data and protocol: retain DATA_DIR=os.environ['GAGC_DATA_DIR'], all four category routes, supplied splits, preprocessing seed 0, training seed 42, single-GPU execution, maximum 200 epochs, and exactly 200 batches per completed epoch. Preserve family-specific sample_batch, baseline loss, optimizer, batch size, and HSTU architecture settings to isolate the embedding change. Write artifacts beneath the trial directory. Do not inspect other trials, test files, unavailable reviews, categories, ratings, prices, or stores. Only permitted public item titles/descriptions and training interactions may inform lexical preprocessing; do not filter or choose vocabulary using validation targets. Use only catalog metadata already supplied by the host, including metadata for candidate IDs when available under its existing policy.

Reproducible lexical defaults: build a separate deterministic vocabulary per category. Apply Unicode NFKC normalization and lowercase; tokenize with the fixed pattern [a-z0-9]+(?:[._/+:-][a-z0-9]+)*, preserving punctuation inside model identifiers and units where this pattern permits. Retain repeated words. Keep at most the first 24 title tokens and first 40 description tokens, concatenate them, and mean-pool their retained embeddings. Use the top 20,000 tokens with occurrence count at least 2, ordering by descending count and lexicographic ties; reserve padding and unknown IDs. Serialize the exact tokenizer version, normalization, token pattern, vocabulary, truncation limits, and item-to-token mapping. These defaults are proposed settings, not literature-established optima. Missing or empty text receives an exactly zero residual.

Embedding design: use token dimension 64, initialized independently from a normal distribution with standard deviation 0.02, a bias-free linear projection into the baseline item dimension, and LayerNorm with elementwise_affine=False and eps=1e-5. Let sigma_ID be the deterministic standard deviation prescribed by the corrected baseline's ID initialization; if the initializer has no scalar standard deviation, calculate and record the initialized nonpadding table's per-coordinate RMS once. Define e(i)=ID(i)+sigmoid(a)*sigma_ID*LN(W*mean(Token(tokens_i))), with a initialized to -3. Apply any baseline embedding multiplier at exactly its original location after the combined lookup. This fixes the earlier scale gap: LayerNorm output has approximately unit variance and could otherwise dominate small ID vectors. Preserve the baseline's output normalization and scoring convention. Zero padding after every transformation; bypass LayerNorm for empty token bags. Include all new trainable parameters in the baseline optimizer with its existing regularization policy, and save the scale as a checkpoint buffer.

Efficient and consistent computation: use EmbeddingBag(mode='mean') with offsets, deduplicate requested item IDs, encode their token bags once, and gather with inverse indices; preserve repeated words within each bag. Never materialize a catalog-by-token-by-dimension tensor. Reuse differentiable embeddings across lookups within a training forward when practical, but never retain their graph across optimizer updates. item_emb must expose forward(item_ids) and an effective weight property representing the same combined embeddings; compute the latter in chunks when diagnostics require the full table. Retain any baseline-required embedding attributes. No detached catalog cache may be used for training. At inference, load the selected weights, call model.eval(), then build chunked effective catalog vectors under torch.inference_mode(). Clear or bypass caches after weight loading, device/dtype changes, or resuming training.

Compatibility and diagnosis: preserve log2feats(sequence), predict_score(features, items), the host ModelView interfaces, and the actual nn.Module in view.model. All candidate and historical representations must come from the same embedding module. Read left-padded histories at the maximum nonpadding index, never count-1; give all-padding rows an explicit zero-feature fallback. Retain DiagnosisProbe(view, device), run_full_diagnosis(train_loader), and diagnosis_interpreter_prompt(raw_diagnosis). The loader contract remains (None, sequence, positive, negative), each tensor B x L. Compute margins with the actual prediction scores on valid positions; measure collapse on effective combined embeddings and state its mapping from cosine similarity. Return metrics and metric_definitions. Mark unavailable metadata breakdowns as unavailable rather than inventing categories or interpreting empty lists as evidence.

Selection and budget: predeclare two configurations: the supplied ID-only baseline and this lexical variant, each trained independently from scratch, one model per category. Use only the host's established validation/checkpoint schedule and stopping rule, documenting them before execution; do not add extra validation queries or alter checkpoint selection. Log configuration, checkpoint epoch, category scores, macro score, and consumed GPU time for every evaluation, including failures. Compare complete four-category configurations using macro validation HR@10; do not assemble a new configuration by cherry-picking categories. Prefer baseline on an exact macro tie and preserve its existing deterministic within-run checkpoint tie-break. Stop within the remaining shared 43,200 GPU-second budget; do not interpret an incomplete configuration as a completed comparison. Freeze one selected checkpoint per category before final held-out evaluation. Every predictor loads exactly one jointly trained category model; no score fusion, checkpoint averaging, or independent experts.

Uncertainty and mechanism checks: one additional hit changes category HR by 0.005 and macro HR by 0.00125. If the existing host interface exposes per-user validation hits, retain paired binary outcomes and compute 10,000 paired bootstrap replicates with RNG seed 42, resampling 200 users within each category and equally averaging category differences. Report the observed macro difference, category differences, and percentile 95% interval. These intervals condition on fixed candidates and checkpoints, exclude training-seed and negative-sampling variability, and do not correct winner-selection bias. If only aggregate HR is exposed, omit paired intervals. For descriptive breakdowns, define training-target-frequency strata as 0-5, 6-20, and at least 21 interactions; define history-target lexical overlap using target tokens and the last five observed history items, separating missing-text cases. Report denominators and avoid causal claims. Brand shortcuts are plausible but not established: brand overlap can reflect legitimate preference. Shuffled-text and deterministic identifiable-brand-token removal controls would strengthen mechanism testing but are deferred beyond the initial two-configuration plan; do not infer brand identities from unavailable fields. Controls, if later authorized within budget, must each be separately trained single networks and never fused.

Deployment: each category's single checkpoint must contain weights, architecture configuration, effective-embedding scale, lexical buffers, and exact vocabulary/tokenizer settings. Update the embedded predictor writer together with the training architecture. Verify round-trip checkpoint loading reproduces scores on fixed synthetic left-padded sequences, including empty histories, missing text, repeated items, and padding. This is a reproducible design specification rather than a safe source patch: the corrected baseline source, exact loader formats, and host checkpoint schedule were not included in the supplied message.
idea.pseudocode:
CONFIGS = [ID_ONLY_BASELINE, JOINT_LEXICAL_HSTU]
# Predeclare both configurations, existing evaluation/stopping schedule, and tie rules.
for config in CONFIGS:
    for category in FOUR_CATEGORIES:
        data = baseline_load_and_split(os.environ['GAGC_DATA_DIR'], category,
                                       preprocessing_seed=0)
        seed_everything(42)
        model = corrected_baseline_HSTU(category_config)
        if config == JOINT_LEXICAL_HSTU:
            vocab, bags, offsets = deterministic_permitted_text_preprocessing(data)
            sigma_id = prescribed_initial_ID_scale_or_recorded_initial_RMS(model)
            model.item_emb = JointLexicalEmbedding(
                original_ID=model.item_emb, token_dim=64, gate_init=-3,
                sigma_id=sigma_id, vocab=vocab, bags=bags, offsets=offsets)
            # e(ids) = ID(ids) + sigmoid(gate)*sigma_id*LN(project(mean_tokens(ids)))
            # Empty-text residual and padding representations are exactly zero.
        optimizer = baseline_optimizer(model.parameters())
        for epoch in range(min(configured_epochs, 200)):
            model.train()  # invalidate inference caches
            for step in range(200):
                _, sequence, positive, negative = family_specific_sample_batch(data)
                features = model.log2feats(sequence)
                loss = unchanged_baseline_loss_using_actual_model_scores(
                    features, positive, negative, model.predict_score)
                optimizer_step(loss)
            run_existing_validation_and_checkpoint_selection_at_existing_schedule()
            if existing_stopping_rule_fires():
                break
        save_selected_single_checkpoint_with_architecture_and_lexical_state(category)
    record_complete_configuration_macro_HR10_and_GPU_cost(config)
selected_config = highest_macro_HR10_complete_configuration(prefer_baseline_on_tie=True)
# Keep its four selected checkpoints; do not choose categories across configurations.
if host_exposes_existing_per_user_hits:
    paired_stratified_bootstrap_stored_hits(replicates=10000, seed=42)
write_predictor_with_identical_HSTU_and_embedding_definitions(selected_config)
verify_serialization_score_equivalence_and_padding_behavior()
# Predictor: route category, load its single checkpoint, model.eval(), build chunked
# catalog embeddings under inference_mode(), and score with that same network.
# Readout index = max(where(sequence != 0, arange(L), -1)); empty rows use zero features.

originality.positive: Tests a constrained, scale-matched lexical adaptation of content-enriched HSTU with all text parameters trained from scratch.
originality.negative: ID-plus-content fusion, gated residuals, and mean token pooling are established techniques; the contribution is a controlled adaptation.

future_potential.positive: A controlled improvement, especially for sparse items and beyond lexical-overlap cases, would motivate inexpensive attribute sharing without pretrained weights.
future_potential.negative: Sparse interaction supervision may learn brand or lexical shortcuts without semantic equivalence, reliable compatibility, or improved full-catalog usefulness.

code_difficulty.positive: The encoder is small and retains the HSTU backbone, sampler, objective, and training protocol.
code_difficulty.negative: Correct scale preservation, effective-weight access, differentiable deduplication, cache invalidation, serialization, and generated-predictor consistency add moderate integration work.

related_work.title: HSTU-BLaIR (2025)
contributions: Investigates enriching HSTU item representations with textual metadata embeddings.
limitations: Uses pretrained BLaIR representations; reported gains do not establish benefits from randomly initialized lexical encoders.

related_work.title: SimRec (2024)
contributions: Uses title-derived similarity distributions to supervise next-item scores.
limitations: Uses pretrained text representations and a SASRec backbone; transfer to this HSTU experiment remains unverified.

related_work.title: Official HSTU sampled-softmax configuration
contributions: Provides an HSTU configuration with 128 sampled negatives and normalized representations.
limitations: MovieLens settings do not establish optimal negative counts or temperatures for these Amazon categories.

related_work.title: Hard-BPR
contributions: Examines false-negative problems associated with hard sampling and motivates a robust ranking objective.
limitations: Does not establish that hard-negative training improves the fixed HSTU Amazon benchmark.

related_work.title: TASTE
contributions: Reports improvements in long-tail recommendation and reduced popularity bias using text-based representations.
limitations: Uses pretrained language representations; its results do not establish gains from the proposed from-scratch mean-pooled token encoder.

related_work.title: Recformer
contributions: Reports strong cold-start and low-resource recommendation results using language representations.
limitations: Its pretraining and architecture differ from the constrained HSTU experiment.

related_work.title: TedRec
contributions: Highlights challenges in directly combining text and ID embeddings with different representation characteristics.
limitations: Does not validate the proposed scale-matched gated residual or guarantee that simple addition will work.

related_work.title: On Sampled Metrics for Item Recommendation
contributions: Shows that sampled evaluation can differ materially from full-catalog evaluation, including model-comparison reversals.
limitations: Does not justify changing the pinned benchmark; conclusions here remain conditional on its fixed candidate protocol.

related_work.title: Statistical Significance Tests for Machine Translation Evaluation
contributions: Provides a reference for paired bootstrap comparison; the proposed category-stratified recommendation analysis is an adaptation.
limitations: Requires paired outcomes and does not account for training variation, candidate variation, or adaptive model selection.

related_work.title: On Over-fitting in Model Selection and Subsequent Selection Bias in Performance Evaluation
contributions: Explains overfitting during model selection and resulting performance-estimation bias.
limitations: A bounded search reduces opportunities for selection overfitting but does not eliminate bias or make ordinary winner intervals post-selection valid.

related_work.title: PyTorch LayerNorm
contributions: Documents normalization and affine parameters relevant to controlling the lexical residual's scale.
limitations: API behavior does not establish the optimal residual magnitude for this task.

related_work.title: PyTorch EmbeddingBag
contributions: Supports pooled token embeddings without materializing intermediate embeddings for every token.
limitations: Empty-bag, offset, padding, and repeated-token behavior must match the serialized preprocessing.

related_work.title: PyTorch torch.unique
contributions: Provides unique IDs and inverse indices for deduplicating item encoding requests.
limitations: Deduplication must apply to requested item IDs rather than removing repeated words from an item's text.

related_work.title: PyTorch inference_mode
contributions: Documents inference-only execution and explicitly distinguishes it from setting model evaluation mode.
limitations: Does not manage cache validity; weight, device, dtype, and training-state changes require explicit invalidation.
